result.rationale: The diff changed `usernames` from a computed property derived from `members` (auto-synced per group) to a plain `usernames: null` property, and the new setupController only does `controller.set("model", model)` without resetting `usernames`. The addMembers action sends `this.get("usernames")` to the newly loaded group's model, so stale input from a previously viewed group would be committed to the current group. The mechanism is consistent with the diff, though controller reuse across route transitions isn't fully provable here.

judged_text: setupController replaces the model but never resets the controller's usernames property, so the add-members selector keeps the text typed while viewing the previous group. An admin who types usernames into group A's add-members field, navigates to group B, and clicks Add commits A's leftover names to B — the stale input is pre-filled with another group's pending members and one click adds them to the wrong group.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin_group_route.js`, `setupController` now only does `controller.set("model", model);` and calls `model.findMembers();` but never clears `controller.usernames`. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `usernames` is a simple mutable property (no longer derived from members), and the template’s add-members `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}` is two-way bound to it. Since Ember commonly reuses the same controller instance when switching models on the same route, the previously typed `usernames` value can persist when navigating to a different group, and `actions.addMembers` will send that stale value to the new group (`this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))`).
